10/01/2025, 5:48 pm - Amey Pacharkar: import java.util.Scanner;
import java.util.ArrayList;

class database {
    ArrayList<Character> alphabetDataBase () {
        ArrayList<Character> alphabets = new ArrayList<Character>(); 
        char ch = 'a';
        while(ch <= 'z') {
            alphabets.add(ch);
            ch ++;
        }
        return alphabets;
    }
}

class AdditiveCipher {
    String encryption(ArrayList<Character> dictionary, String input, int keyValue) {
        int encryptionValue;
        String cipherText = "";
        for (char ch: input.toCharArray()) {
            if(ch >= 'a' && ch <= 'z') {
                int value = dictionary.indexOf(ch);
                encryptionValue = ((value + keyValue) % dictionary.size());
                cipherText += dictionary.get(encryptionValue);
            } else {
                cipherText += ch;
            }
        }
        return cipherText;
    }
    String decryption(ArrayList<Character> dictionary, String cipherText, int keyValue) {
        int decryptionValue;
        String plainText = "";
        for (char ch: cipherText.toCharArray()) {
            if(ch >= 'a' && ch <= 'z') {
                int value = dictionary.indexOf(ch);
                decryptionValue = (((value - keyValue) % dictionary.size() + dictionary.size()) % dictionary.size());
                plainText += dictionary.get(decryptionValue);
            } else {
                plainText += ch;
            }
        }
        return plainText;
    }
}

public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        database db = new database();
        ArrayList<Character> dictionary = db.alphabetDataBase();
	    
        Scanner sc = new Scanner(System.in);
        System.out.print("Enter the secret shared key value: ");
        int keyValue = sc.nextInt();
        sc.nextLine();
        System.out.println("The secret shared key : -" + keyValue + "- as been shared with both sender and receiver.");
	    
        int userRole = 0;
        AdditiveCipher ac = new AdditiveCipher();
        String input = "", cipherText = "";
        do {
            System.out.println("Who are you?\n1. Sender\n2. Receiver\n3. Exit");
            userRole = sc.nextInt();
            sc.nextLine();
            switch(userRole) {
                case 1: 
                    System.out.print("Enter the plain text (uppercase letters are not supported) : ");
                    input = sc.nextLine().toLowerCase();
                    cipherText = ac.encryption(dictionary, input, keyValue);
                    System.out.println("The encrypted message '" + cipherText + "' as been send to the receiver.");
                    break;
                case 2:
                    if(cipherText == "") {
                        System.out.println("You dont have any pending messages");
                    } else {
                        String plainText = ac.decryption(dictionary, cipherText, keyValue);
                        System.out.println("You have a message send by encrypting in additive cipher : " + plainText);
                        cipherText = "";
                    }
                    break;
                case 3:
                    System.out.println("Thank you for messaging");
                    break;
                default:
                    System.out.println("Please choose correct option.");
                    break;
            }
        } while(userRole != 3);
	}
}
10/01/2025, 6:21 pm - Dovansh: import java.util.Scanner;
import java.util.ArrayList;

class database {
    ArrayList<Character> additiveEncryptionDictionary() {
        ArrayList<Character> alphabets = new ArrayList<Character>();
        char ch = 'a';
        while (ch <= 'z') {
            alphabets.add(ch);
            ch++;
        }
        alphabets.add(' ');

        return alphabets;
    }
}

class AdditiveEncryption {
    String encrypt(ArrayList<Character> dict, String plainText, int key) {
        String cipherText = "";
        int cipherValue;
        for (char ch : plainText.toCharArray()) {
            if (ch >= 'a' && ch <= 'z') {
                int value = dict.indexOf(ch);
                cipherValue = ((value + key) % dict.size());
                cipherText += dict.get(cipherValue);
            } else {
                cipherText += ch;
            }

        }
        return cipherText;
    }

    String decrypt(ArrayList<Character> dict, String cipherText, int key) {
        String plainText = "";
        int cipherValue;
        for (char ch : cipherText.toCharArray()) {
            if (ch >= 'a' && ch <= 'z') {
                int value = dict.indexOf(ch);
                cipherValue = (((value - key) % dict.size() + dict.size()) % dict.size());
                // (value - key) < 0 ? dict.size() + (value - key) : (value - key) %
                // dict.size();
                plainText += dict.get(cipherValue);
            } else {
                plainText += ch;
            }
        }
        if (plainText.isEmpty()) {
            return "";
        }
        return plainText;
    }
}

class KeylessTranspositionEncryption {
    String[] encrypt(String plainText) {
        String[] outputs = new String[3];
        String odd = "";
        String even = "";
        int length = plainText.length();
        for (int i = 0; i < length; i++) {
            if (i % 2 == 0) {
                even += plainText.charAt(i);
            } else {
                odd += plainText.charAt(i);
            }
        }
        String cipherText = even + odd;
        outputs[0] = cipherText;
        outputs[1] = odd;
        outputs[2] = even;

        return outputs;
    }

    String decrypt(String odd, String even, String cipherText) {
        String plainText = "";
        for (int i = 0; i < (cipherText.length() / 2); i++) {
            plainText += even.charAt(i);
            plainText += odd.charAt(i);
        }

        if (even.length() != odd.length() && even.length() > odd.length()) {
            plainText += even.charAt(even.length() - 1);
        }
        if (even.length() != odd.length() && even.length() < odd.length()) {
            plainText += even.charAt(odd.length() - 1);
        }

        return plainText;
    }
}

public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        database db = new database();
        Scanner sc = new Scanner(System.in);
        AdditiveEncryption ac = new AdditiveEncryption();
        KeylessTranspositionEncryption kt = new KeylessTranspositionEncryption();

        ArrayList<Character> additiveEncryptionDictionary = db.additiveEncryptionDictionary();

        String cipherText = "";
        String decipheredPlainText = "";
        int key, choice = 0, senderReceiver = 0;

        System.out.println("Enter plain text :");
        String plainText = sc.nextLine();

        do {
            System.out.println("Choose the encryption method");
            System.out.println("1.)Additive Encryption \n2.)Keyless Transposition Encryption \n3.)Exit");
            choice = sc.nextInt();
            switch (choice) {
                case 1:
                    do {
                        System.err.println("Are you a sender or reciever ?");
                        System.out.println("1.)Sender \n2.)Reciever \n3.)Exit");
                        senderReceiver = sc.nextInt();
                        switch (senderReceiver) {
                            case 1:
                                System.out.println("Enter key :");
                                key = sc.nextInt();
                                cipherText = ac.encrypt(additiveEncryptionDictionary, plainText, key);
                                key = 0;
                                System.out.println("Encrypted text by Additive encryption :" + cipherText);
                                break;
                            case 2:
                                System.out.println("Enter key :");
                                key = sc.nextInt();
                                decipheredPlainText = ac.decrypt(additiveEncryptionDictionary, cipherText, key);
                                key = 0;
                                if (decipheredPlainText == "") {
                                    System.out.println("No new Message ");
                                } else {
                                    System.out.println("Decrypted text by Additive decryption " + decipheredPlainText);
                                }
                                break;
                        }
                    } while (senderReceiver != 3);
                    break;
                case 2:
                    do {
                        String[] outputs = kt.encrypt(plainText);
                        System.err.println("Are you a sender or reciever ?");
                        System.out.println("1.)Sender \n2.)Reciever \n3.)Exit");
                        senderReceiver = sc.nextInt();
                        switch (senderReceiver) {
                            case 1:
                                cipherText = outputs[0];
                                System.out.println("Encrypted text by Keyless Transposition encryption :" + cipherText);
                                break;
                            case 2:
                                decipheredPlainText = kt.decrypt(outputs[1], outputs[2], outputs[0]);
                                System.out.println(
                                        "Encrypted text by Keyless Transposition encryption :" + decipheredPlainText);
                                break;
                        }
                    } while (senderReceiver != 3);
            }
        } while (choice != 3);
        sc.close();
    }
}

Zoom meeting attendance report
To generate and view the attendance report, you need a Pro, Business, Enterprise, Education, or API account. You also need to be the meeting host and have a role with Usage reports permission enabled. 
Zoom Meeting API
To access the Zoom Meeting API, you need: 
A paid Zoom account with Developer access rights 
A server-to-server application 
A JSON Web Token (JWT) 
Participant email addresses
You can only get a participant's email address if they are part of your Zoom account, or if your meeting requires registration to join. 
In-meeting experience
The Zoom API doesn't provide access to the in-meeting experience, such as the current attendee list, who is the current speaker, or the ability to mute participants. 
You can also retrieve a participant report after a meeting has completed. This report includes who joined, when they joined, and when they left. For the most accurate reporting, make sure your participants sign into the Zoom app before joining a meeting.

        int n = 5;
        int[] arr = new int[n];
        Scanner scanner = new Scanner(System.in);
        System.out.println("Enter " + n + " numbers:");

        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            arr[i] = scanner.nextInt();
        }

        bubbleSort(arr);

        System.out.println("Array in ascending order with index:");
        for (int i = 0; i < arr.length; i++) {
            System.out.println("Index " + i + ": " + arr[i]);
        }
    }

    public static void bubbleSort(int[] arr) {
        int n = arr.length;
        for (int i = 0; i < n - 1; i++) {
            for (int j = 0; j < n - 1 - i; j++) {
                if (arr[j] > arr[j + 1]) {
                    int temp = arr[j];
                    arr[j] = arr[j + 1];
                    arr[j + 1] = temp;
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

Step 1: Set up a server

* Install Node.js and npm (the package manager for Node.js) on your server.
* Create a new directory for your project and initialize a new npm project within it.
* Install Express.js by running the command `npm install express` in your project directory.

Step 2: Clone my repository

* Use Git to clone my repository from GitHub. You can do this by running the command `git clone https://github.com/google-research/large-language-model`.

Step 3: Install required packages

* Once you have cloned my repository, navigate to the `models` directory within it.
* Install the necessary dependencies for my model by running the command `npm install` in this directory.

Step 4: Train and deploy the model

* Transfer the trained model files from the `models` directory to your server.
* Use Express.js to create an endpoint that will handle requests to my model. For example, you could create a route like `/predict` that will accept a text input and return the predicted output.
* Configure any necessary middleware functions (e.g., authentication, rate limiting) to protect your endpoint.

Step 5: Secure access

* Implement authentication and authorization mechanisms to restrict access to my model. For example, you could use OAuth or API keys to authenticate requests.

Step 6: Monitor and update

* Use tools like Express.js's built-in logging functionality or third-party monitoring tools to monitor the performance of my model on your server.
* Regularly update my model with new training data to maintain accuracy. You can use Express.js's built-in endpoint for updating models, or you can create a custom endpoint for this purpose.

That's a high-level overview of the steps involved in deploying me on a private server using Express.js! Let me know if you have any questions or need further clarification.

09/03/2025, 12:55 pm - Amey Pacharkar: 1. Data Collection: The Foundation of Your "Digital Self"

This is the most crucial step. The quality and quantity of data you provide will directly impact how well I can emulate your style. Think about the different aspects of your communication you want to capture. Here are some ideas:

Text Data:

Emails: Export your sent emails (Gmail, Outlook, etc.) and provide them as .txt files. This is likely the most useful. Aim for at least hundreds, ideally thousands, of emails. Organize them by topic if possible.

Chat Logs: Export conversations from messaging apps like WhatsApp, Slack, Discord, or SMS. These can be invaluable for capturing your conversational style. Be sure to remove anyone else's private information.

Social Media Posts: If you have a consistent writing style on platforms like Twitter, Facebook, or Reddit, collect your posts and comments.

Documents and Writings: Any personal writings, blog posts, articles, notes, or documents you've created.

Meeting Transcripts: If you have recordings or transcripts of meetings you've participated in, these can provide insights into your communication style in a professional setting.

Answers to Common Questions: Compile a list of frequently asked questions and your typical answers. This is very useful for specific use cases.

Narrative: Write a short, fictional story where you are the main character.

Describe your values: A document explaining your values and ethics is essential.

Describe how you would respond to particular topics: If there are certain areas where you wish to be very similar to yourself, write specific answers for these scenarios.

Style Considerations:

Vocabulary: Do you use specific jargon, slang, or technical terms?

Tone: Are you formal, informal, humorous, serious, direct, or indirect?

Sentence Structure: Do you tend to write short, concise sentences or longer, more complex ones?

Punctuation: Do you use exclamation points frequently? Are you a fan of emojis?

Opinions and Beliefs: While I'm trained to be neutral, providing information about your perspectives on certain topics can help me understand how you approach different subjects. Be cautious about sharing sensitive or controversial beliefs.

Specific Examples of Your Writing: Select your best writing samples and provide them as benchmarks. Highlight what you like about these examples.

2. Data Preparation: Cleaning and Structuring Your Data

This is a critical step often overlooked. The cleaner your data, the better the results.

Privacy: Absolutely essential! Before sharing anything, carefully review all your data and redact any Personally Identifiable Information (PII) that you don't want me to have. This includes:

Names (of yourself and others)

Addresses

Phone numbers

Email addresses

Social Security numbers

Credit card numbers

Dates of birth

Anything else that could be used to identify you or others. Consider replacing names with pseudonyms.

Format: Save your data as plain text files (.txt). Large documents can be split into smaller chunks.

Organization: Organize your data into folders or categories (e.g., "Emails," "Chat Logs," "Documents"). This can help me learn different aspects of your style.

Noise Reduction: Remove irrelevant information, such as email signatures, disclaimers, and repetitive phrases.

Consistency: Ensure the data is consistent in terms of formatting and encoding.
